questions.stem: An importer keeps `private IOException firstFailure;` and ends `importAll() throws IOException` with `if (failed) throw firstFailure;`. Because of a bug, one kind of bad row sets `failed = true` without ever assigning `firstFailure`. A file containing only that kind of bad row is imported. What does the caller of importAll() get?

options.text: A NullPointerException, since the throw statement evaluates its operand and finds no object to throw
options.says: the operand of throw is evaluated at run time; when it is null, the throw itself fails with NullPointerException

options.text: An IOException with no message, since the JVM creates an instance of the field's declared type
options.says: nothing creates an exception for you; the throw fails with NullPointerException

options.text: No exception, since a throw whose operand is null is skipped and importAll() returns normally
options.says: a throw never completes normally; with a null operand it throws NullPointerException

options.text: No program to run, since the compiler rejects throwing a field that may still be null
options.says: the compiler only requires a Throwable type; whether the value is null is found out at run time

origin.section: The Compiler Knows a `throw` Ends the Block; It Doesn't Know Your Helper Always Throws

questions.stem: `int parsePort(String s)` parses `s` into `n`, then ends with `if (n >= 1 && n <= 65535) return n;` followed by `rejectPort(s);`. `static void rejectPort(String s)` has a single statement, `throw new IllegalArgumentException("bad port: " + s);`. What happens when the class is built and parsePort("70000") is called?

options.text: It builds, and the call throws IllegalArgumentException, since rejectPort can never return to parsePort
options.says: the compiler checks parsePort against rejectPort's void signature, not its body, so it reports a missing return

options.text: It builds, and the call returns 0, since an int method that runs off its end returns the default value
options.says: Java has no implicit return value; a path without return in an int method is a compile error

options.text: It doesn't build, since the compiler sees only that rejectPort returns void and finds a path with no return
options.says: the compiler knows a throw statement ends the block, but not that a called method always throws; it reports missing return statement

options.text: It doesn't build, since a method that always throws must declare its exception in a throws clause
options.says: IllegalArgumentException is unchecked and needs no throws clause; the error is the missing return in parsePort

origin.section: The Compiler Knows a `throw` Ends the Block; It Doesn't Know Your Helper Always Throws

questions.stem: `Stream<Invoice> parseAll(List<Path> files) throws IOException` returns `files.stream().map(...)`, where the lambda wraps any IOException in an UncheckedIOException, all inside a try whose `catch (UncheckedIOException e)` rethrows `e.getCause()`. A caller writes `try { parseAll(files).forEach(this::book); } catch (IOException e) { alert(e); }`, and the second file is missing. What does the caller see?

options.text: Its catch gets the NoSuchFileException, since parseAll's catch unwraps it as forEach reads the files
options.says: the files are read only when forEach runs, after parseAll's try has ended, so nothing unwraps the failure

options.text: Its catch gets the NoSuchFileException, since parseAll reads all the files before forEach starts
options.says: a stream without a terminal operation reads nothing; the reading happens in the caller's forEach

options.text: An UncheckedIOException escapes past its catch, since forEach reads the files after parseAll returns
options.says: the lazy stream runs the lambda during the caller's forEach, outside the try that would have unwrapped it

options.text: A NoSuchFileException escapes past its catch, since forEach can't pass a checked exception to a catch
options.says: the wrapper escapes, not the IOException; and a checked exception that reaches a matching catch is caught as usual

origin.section: A Checked Exception Can't Leave a `Function`: Wrap It in the Lambda, Unwrap It at Your Boundary

questions.stem: A library method `List<Row> Rows.fetchAll(Connection c)` has no throws clause, but uses a generic sneaky-throw helper so that an SQLException from its internal lambdas escapes from it unwrapped. Your code calls it inside `try { ... } catch (SQLException e) { retryLater(); }`. What happens?

options.text: It compiles, and the catch runs, since what arrives at run time really is an SQLException
options.says: the catch never gets that far: the compiler rejects it because nothing in the try body declares SQLException

options.text: It compiles, and the catch never runs, since the helper turns the SQLException into a RuntimeException
options.says: the erased cast changes nothing at run time; the SQLException itself arrives, and the catch doesn't compile anyway

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a catch for a checked exception the try body can't throw is an error
options.says: the compiler sees no SQLException in fetchAll's signature and reports that it is never thrown in the try body

options.text: It doesn't compile, since your method has to declare SQLException in a throws clause first
options.says: declaring it on your method doesn't help; the error is the catch for an exception the try body can't throw

origin.section: A Sneaky Throw Compiles, and Leaves Callers Unable to Name What It Throws
